{{short description|Plot of a dynamical system's trajectories in phase space}}
{{Differential equations}}
[[File:Pendulum phase portrait.svg|thumb|312x312px|[[Potential energy]] and phase portrait of a [[simple pendulum]]. Note that the x-axis, being angular, wraps onto itself after every 2π radians.]]
[[File:Phase portrait of damped oscillator, with increasing damping strength.gif|thumb|Phase portrait of damped oscillator, with increasing damping strength. The equation of motion is <math>\ddot x + 2\gamma \dot x + \omega^2 x = 0.</math>]]

In [[mathematics]], a '''phase portrait''' is a geometric representation of the [[orbit (dynamics)|orbit]]s of a [[dynamical system]] in the [[phase plane]]. Each set of initial conditions is represented by a different [[Point (geometry)|point]] or [[curve]].

Phase portraits are an invaluable tool in studying dynamical systems. They consist of a [[plot (graphics)|plot]] of typical trajectories in the [[phase space]]. This reveals information such as whether an [[attractor]], a [[repellor]] or [[limit cycle]] is present for the chosen parameter value. The concept of [[topological conjugacy|topological equivalence]] is important in classifying the behaviour of systems by specifying when two different phase portraits represent the same qualitative dynamic behavior. An attractor is a stable point which is also called a "sink". The repeller is considered as an unstable point, which is also known as a "source".

A phase portrait graph of a dynamical system depicts the system's trajectories (with arrows) and stable [[steady state]]s (with dots) and unstable steady states (with circles) in a phase space. The axes are of [[state variable]]s.

[[File:Van_der_pols_equation_phase_portrait.svg|right|300px|thumb|Phase portrait of [[Van der Pol oscillator|van der Pol's equation]], <math>\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}+\mu(y^2-1)\frac{dy}{dt}+y=0</math>.]]

*[[Simple pendulum]], see picture (right).
*Simple [[harmonic oscillator]] where the phase portrait is made up of ellipses centred at the origin, which is a fixed point.
*[[Damped harmonic motion]], see animation (right).
*[[Van der Pol oscillator]] see picture (bottom right).

== Visualizing the behavior of ordinary differential equations ==
A phase portrait represents the directional behavior of a system of [[ordinary differential equation]]s (ODEs). The phase portrait can indicate the stability of the system.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Haynes |author-link=Haynes Miller |last2=Mattuck |first2=Arthur |author-link2=Arthur Mattuck |date=Spring 2010 |title=Supplementary Notes to Chapter 26 |url=https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-03-differential-equations-spring-2010/resources/mit18_03s10_chapter_26/ |access-date=2024-12-28 |website=MIT OpenCourseWare |language=en}} </ref>
{| class="wikitable"
|+Stability<ref name=":0" />
|Unstable
|Most of the system's solutions tend towards ∞ over time
|-
|Asymptotically stable
|All of the system's solutions tend to 0 over time
|-
|Neutrally stable
|None of the system's solutions tend towards ∞ over time, but most solutions do not tend towards 0 either
|}
The phase portrait behavior of a system of ODEs can be determined by the [[eigenvalue]]s or the [[Trace (linear algebra)|trace]] and [[determinant]] ({{nobr|1=trace = λ<sub>1</sub> + λ<sub>2</sub>}}, {{nobr|1=determinant = λ<sub>1</sub>λ<sub>2</sub>}}) of the system.<ref name=":0" />
{| class="wikitable"
|+Phase portrait behavior<ref name=":0" />
!Eigenvalue, trace, determinant
!Phase portrait shape
|-
|λ<sub>1</sub> and λ<sub>2</sub> are real and of opposite sign;<br/> Determinant < 0
|Saddle (unstable)
|-
|λ<sub>1</sub> and λ<sub>2</sub> are real and of the same sign, and λ<sub>1</sub> ≠ λ<sub>2</sub>;<br/> 0 < determinant < (trace<sup>2</sup> / 4)
|Node (stable if trace < 0, unstable if trace > 0)
|-
|λ<sub>1</sub> and λ<sub>2</sub> have both a real and imaginary component;<br/> (trace<sup>2</sup> / 4) < determinant
|Spiral (stable if trace < 0, unstable if trace > 0)
|}
